expansion: Probably no: on the fixed 4x79 control and the fixed 167/80 obstruction, exact tail completion should be decidable by a sufficiently rich finite residual signature without true pushdown memory.
The hard part is not formal expressivity but state width: any small static boundary-debt summary aliases too many prefixes.
A stack only survives if it compresses that residual signature or reuses proof information better than a matched non-stack baseline.

associations.cue: global boundary width on odd cycles
expansion: Write n = 2h + 1. For a prefix cut at t and a shift k, the future cross-boundary pairs touch prefix indices [0, k - 1] and [t - k, t - 1].
Union over k = 1..h gives [0, h - 1] union [t - h, t - 1]. Because t <= 2h = n - 1, that union covers every prefix index.
So for the concrete panels here, h = 39 for n = 79 and h = 83 for n = 167, and every prefix bit remains exposed to the tail until the end. There is no narrow local frontier.
Each fixed-n exact tail language is finite and therefore regular once n, the target autocorrelation vector, and the target weight are fixed.
That means a pushdown automaton is not forced by expressivity on a single panel; it is only one way to encode the residual information.
If a stack matters, it has to win on compactness, transfer, or proof reuse, not on necessity.

associations.cue: VPA fit check from the literature
expansion: Visibly pushdown automata are most natural when the alphabet itself exposes call, return, and internal symbols and therefore visible nesting.

The raw support words for the 4x79 and 167/80 panels do not come with that structure. Any push, pop, and no-op discipline would be imposed by our tokenization, not read off the exact cyclic equations.
That makes pushdown a modeling choice rather than an obvious structural match.

associations.cue: SAT+CAS and programmatic SAT as the stronger adjacent precedent
expansion: The closest exact-search neighbors for Williamson and Golay style problems push information forward as clauses, propagators, and reusable nogoods rather than as stack frames.
That points to proof-carrying feedback as the more plausible improvement over a static summary.
If stack memory helps only after exact failures are turned into reusable vetoes, the credit belongs mostly to adaptive proof reuse, not to pushdown expressivity.
Canonical orbit words are still useful because they quotient cyclic and reversal duplicates before any exact completion step.
But canonicalization does not shrink the exact frontier width: after symmetry removal, every prefix bit can still influence future cross-correlation obligations.
So canonicalization is a fairness requirement for the panel, not evidence that a stack is required.
The solved 4x79 control is the decisive panel for necessity tests because it has a known exact completion under the same odd-cycle geometry.
The unresolved 167/80 target can measure pruning, oracle-call savings, and lower-bound behavior, but it cannot by itself certify that a stack is necessary.
Any necessity claim should survive witness-retention checks on 4x79 and smaller solved same-template controls first.
A non-stack exact baseline can memoize position, used weight, realized autocorrelation debt, and an exposed-prefix signature equivalent to the whole prefix.
That baseline may be very large, but it is the right falsifier: if it matches the stack on witness retention and exact-tail calls, the stack is ornamental.
The real question is whether stack factorization compresses the residual signature enough to matter.

associations.cue: where a stack could still be defensible
expansion: A stack becomes more plausible only after the prefix is re-tokenized into nested dyadic intervals, run blocks, or parseable motifs whose debts naturally compose by push and pop operations.
That would make the stack an implementation of hierarchical convolution bookkeeping, not a requirement of exact tail completion on the raw 79- or 167-step panels.
The burden then shifts to showing better transfer across 4xp controls or fewer exact-oracle calls under a matched baseline.

forced_bridges.from: Convolution numbers: the cyclic case and the exact 167/80 obstruction
forced_bridges.to: domain-independent dynamic programming over residual signatures
forced_bridges.mechanism: Model prefix extendability as a Bellman state whose sufficient data are position, used weight, realized debt, and an exposed-prefix signature. This turns the bottleneck into state compression rather than stack necessity.

forced_bridges.from: exact tail-completion predicate on a fixed panel
forced_bridges.mechanism: Treat two prefixes as equivalent only when every legal tail completes or fails them in the same way. If the minimized finite automaton is already enough, the pushdown story collapses.

Let the static summary do the exact residual bookkeeping, then use failed completions to add reusable nogoods, transition vetoes, or weighted penalties. This tests whether proof objects matter more than stack depth.

forced_bridges.from: raw support words on Z_79 and Z_167
forced_bridges.to: visibly pushdown over dyadic or run-length interval tokens
forced_bridges.mechanism: Impose a hierarchical tokenization whose parse tree is explicit, then let pushes represent entering a block and pops represent closing it while merging deferred convolution debt. If the hierarchy does not buy compression, retire the stack.

forced_bridges.to: active automata learning and regularity-collapse tests
forced_bridges.mechanism: Use exact extendability labels on control prefixes to learn the smallest useful recognizer. If the learned acceptor quickly compiles down to a DFA, the stack was never doing indispensable work.

Reinterpret the residual state as a glue signature carried by a partially assembled object. This stresses the same question from a different angle: is the exact interface finite and static, or does it really need unbounded nested memory?

anomaly_results.constraint: Force the summary to be only position, used weight, and the current realized debt vector
anomaly_results.result: This is too weak for exactness. Two prefixes can share those aggregates while differing in which specific exposed bits still participate in future cross-boundary pairs. Exactness will leak through aliasing even on the solved 4x79 control.

anomaly_results.constraint: Flatten any proposed stack into its exact residual state on a fixed panel
anomaly_results.result: Exactness should survive, which is the strongest evidence against stack necessity. The likely cost is state explosion, not loss of correctness.

anomaly_results.constraint: Impose a nested tokenization and then run a regularity-collapse test
anomaly_results.result: If the accepted frontier compiles to a DFA or if stack depth never carries information beyond a finite signature, the visibly pushdown formulation is cosmetic. This is a realistic failure mode, not a corner case.

anomaly_results.constraint: Evaluate only on the unresolved 167/80 obstruction
anomaly_results.result: You can still measure pruning, lower bounds, and exact-oracle savings, but you cannot prove that a stack is necessary because there is no known witness family on that panel to audit false negatives against.

anomaly_results.constraint: Require zero false negatives on all witness prefixes of the 4x79 control
anomaly_results.result: This becomes the decisive necessity test. If a flattened residual-state baseline passes the same test and rejects a similar share of random prefixes, the stack has no surviving claim.

anomaly_results.constraint: Give the stack access to exact-solver feedback but compare it to a static summary without that feedback
anomaly_results.result: The comparison becomes invalid. Any observed gain could come from learned nogoods or user-propagator style conflict reuse rather than from pushdown memory.

anomaly_results.constraint: Ask for one recognizer that transfers across multiple 4xp controls instead of only a fixed n
anomaly_results.result: This is the one regime where a hierarchical stack becomes more defensible. Uniform transfer across sizes may benefit from recursive token structure even when exactness on each fixed panel remains finite-state.

steering_directions.direction: Residual-signature exact baseline on the 4x79 control
steering_directions.rationale: This directly answers the bottleneck. If an exact non-stack residual signature can match the best pushdown candidate on the solved control, then stack memory is not required for the panel.
steering_directions.first_step: Implement a tail oracle that memoizes prefixes by position, used weight, realized debt, and an exposed-prefix signature equivalent to the whole prefix after canonicalization.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Exact witness-prefix retention is perfect on 4x79, and the measured gap between stack and flat residual-state search shrinks to compression and runtime rather than correctness.

steering_directions.direction: Matched stack-versus-flat ablation on one canonical tokenization
steering_directions.rationale: The only honest way to test stack necessity is to hold tokenization, oracle, and canonicalization fixed and change only the memory discipline.
steering_directions.first_step: Pick one canonical path or run-length encoding, implement both a stack version and a flattened residual-state version, and run them on identical 4x79 prefix panels before touching 167/80.
steering_directions.expected_signal: If stack removal leaves witness retention, rejected-prefix rate, and exact-oracle calls almost unchanged, the answer is no.

steering_directions.direction: Proof-carrying static summary instead of deeper memory
steering_directions.rationale: Adjacent exact-search literature suggests the useful increment over a static summary is reusable conflict information, not an intrinsic need for pushdown state.
steering_directions.first_step: Wrap the flat residual-state baseline around a small exact completion solver, record failed completions, and compress them into short reusable motifs or transition vetoes.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Exact-oracle calls drop materially at fixed witness retention, which would outperform a static summary without needing to claim stack necessity.

steering_directions.direction: Hierarchical tokenization only as a transfer experiment
steering_directions.rationale: A stack is most defensible when it carries recursively composable interval debt across problem sizes, not when it is merely another way to store one fixed panel's residual state.
steering_directions.first_step: Define a dyadic or run-length interval grammar shared by smaller solved 4xp controls, the 4x79 control, and the 167/80 obstruction, then test whether the same stack discipline transfers.
steering_directions.expected_signal: Cross-order transfer appears in learned or hand-built transitions; if not, the hierarchy is decorative.

steering_directions.direction: No-narrow-frontier theorem as an admission gate
steering_directions.rationale: Before building any frontier method, formalize that the exact cyclic half-correlation cut for n = 79 and n = 167 exposes the whole prefix. That prevents accidental overclaiming about local boundary summaries.
steering_directions.first_step: Write the exposed-index derivation [0, h - 1] union [t - h, t - 1] and verify computationally for all t < 79 and t < 167 that every prefix bit stays live.
steering_directions.expected_signal: The design conversation shifts from local boundary bookkeeping to global residual compression, which is the real bottleneck.

validation_checks.direction: Residual-signature exact baseline on the 4x79 control
checks: Exactness check: every prefix along the known 4x79 witness path is accepted by the oracle-backed baseline.
Suffix check: for short-tail slices, exhaustive tail enumeration agrees with the memoized baseline on every sampled prefix.
Width check: report state counts by depth to see whether the residual signature is nearly one-to-one with raw prefixes.

validation_checks.direction: Matched stack-versus-flat ablation on one canonical tokenization
checks: Fairness check: freeze canonicalization, tokenization, and exact-oracle budget across both variants.
Retention check: compare false-negative rates on all 4x79 witness prefixes and on smaller solved same-template controls.
Utility check: compare rejected random-prefix share, exact-oracle calls, and wall time; kill the stack if the flat version matches it.

validation_checks.direction: Proof-carrying static summary instead of deeper memory
checks: Locality check: learned nogoods or vetoes must compress to short motifs or state conditions rather than whole-instance clauses.
Reuse check: the same learned objects must fire on held-out prefixes, not only on the failures that created them.
Performance check: oracle calls and wall time drop at unchanged witness retention.

validation_checks.direction: Hierarchical tokenization only as a transfer experiment
checks: Transfer check: the same stack discipline must retain witness prefixes on multiple solved 4xp controls, not just on one hand-tuned order.
Collapse check: try compiling the accepted frontier to a DFA or an explicit finite summary; if this succeeds with little loss, drop the pushdown claim.
Ablation check: remove hierarchical push and pop bookkeeping while keeping the tokenization fixed; if performance holds, the stack is decorative.

validation_checks.direction: No-narrow-frontier theorem as an admission gate
checks: Derivation check: verify symbolically that the exposed prefix for half-correlation shifts is [0, h - 1] union [t - h, t - 1].
Panel check: verify computationally for n = 79 and n = 167 that all prefix bits remain exposed for every t < n.
Design check: reject any claimed exact boundary summary that inspects only a small local window unless it is explicitly paired with a proof of equivalence to the full residual signature.

sub_problem: Does any exact tail-completion panel for the 4x79 control or the 167/80 obstruction require stack memory beyond a static boundary-debt summary?
